**Background:** UN creates new committee to run the moon, rapidly selling off plots of land for people to colonize

**Goal:** Build an interactive map of the moon that assigns property values to different regions based on various criteria.

**Intended User:** General public, students, and other people generally interested in space but with little to no experience. Intentionally novel product to get people interested in learning more about lunar missions

**Criteria:**

- Temperature range/average temperature  
- Earth communication reliability  
- Terrain/potential hazards  
- Nearby landmarks/cool terrain features

**UI:**

1. Should be general parody of zillow UI, follow similar design with hovering clickable price values above different regions. Left column is lunar map with labeled property values, right column is data on highlighted property  
2. Filter by arbitrary “price” or by different land types  
3. Overlay togglable gradients of:  
   1. Temperature  
   2. Solar Power Generation potential  
   3. Communication Strength  
   4. Lighting Characteristics  
   5. Terrain Hazards  
   6. Viability Score (evaluation function)  
   7. Communication window (would be binary for a given point in time, not a gradient)

**Data:**  
Necessary Systems:

1. Determine safety factor of physical candidate landing sites  
   1. Determine if it is physically possible to land on a site (space, slant of the ground, are there any hazards such as chasms, mountains, cliffs).  
2. System to figure available solar power generation potential at candidate landing sites at times throughout the year, goal is to maximize the amount of solar energy available in an area over the given time period  
   ![][image1]  
   W/M \= atmospheric pressure (between 1412 and 1320 depending on Earth position  
3. System for onsite temperature conditions and potential temperature hazards![][image2][https\://www\.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S009457652500517X](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S009457652500517X), Measuring the temperature on the moon equation. T \= time, Z \= latitude, T() \= temp, K() \= thermal conductivity.  
4. System to determine communication capabilities of the site over time \- account for NASA deep space network somehow (simple LOS with Earth), goal is to minimize time spent without comms for the given landing site  
5. Effort to get to LANDING SITE \- VERY FAR OFF probably not possible (this includes fuel consumption, is it possible to get to the site from earth in a given launch window)  
6. 

## Data Sources

- Sun and earth/moon and earth relative location data:  
  - https\://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api?format=text\&COMMAND='\<destination\>'\&OBJ\_DATA='NO'\&MAKE\_EPHEM='YES'\&EPHEM\_TYPE='VECTORS'\&CENTER='500@399'\&START\_TIME=\<start\_time\>'\&STOP\_TIME=\<stop\_time\>\&STEP\_SIZE='1d'\&OUT\_UNITS='AU-D'\&VEC\_TABLE='3'  
  - Returns a list of distances between the geocenter and the earth over a range of time. RG is the exact distance in AU.  
  - Destination: ‘10’ \- Sun, ‘301’ \- Moon  
- Moon topography map: [https\://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Lunar\_LRO\_LOLA\_Global\_LDEM\_118m\_Mar2014.tif](https://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Lunar_LRO_LOLA_Global_LDEM_118m_Mar2014.tif) (Moon DEM Digital Elevation Model)  
- Quick map of moon:   
- Moon trek: [https\://trek.nasa.gov/tiles/apidoc/trekAPI.html?body=moon](https://trek.nasa.gov/tiles/apidoc/trekAPI.html?body=moon)  
- Data about celestial bodies, api request documentation VERY IMPORTANT: [https\://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api.html](https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api.html)

### Physical Landing Site Safety Factor

#### **Description:**

This system determines the viability of a landing site based on a topographical map and other material conditions at the landing site over time \- mostly slope vs smoothness of candidate landing sites across the moon

### Landing Site Power Generation Potential Evaluator

#### **Description:**

Determine power generation potential of a region and encompassing landing sites 

- Needs to keep track of how long the region is in the sun and how long periods of darkness are   
- Keep track of how much power is available and how much the site is estimated to generate over the time space of a selected mission

## Moon to Earth Communication Windows

Assuming communication with the south pole specifically:  
Horizons query: COMMAND='399'  EPHEM\_TYPE='OBSERVER'  CENTER='coord@301'  COORD\_TYPE='GEODETIC'  
SITE\_COORD='0,-89.9,0'  QUANTITIES='4'  ELEV\_CUT='\<elevation cut\>'  
START\_TIME='\<start\_time\>'  STOP\_TIME=’stop-time'  STEP\_SIZE='1h'

\<elevation\_cut\> is the elevation limit of the antenna, measured in degrees  
south pole is in communication range when elevation is above \<elevation\_cut\>
